label: weak conjunction: t=3-5 after "i" in sequences starting with "x"
explanation: Very sparse feature: about 0.03% of steps. It fires only in the original phase at t=3-6 (mostly t=4) and on the delimiter of short sequences, and never in the copy phase. Activation is spread across several cues that each raise the rate without being needed: first token x (18x lift), previous token i (20x) or 3, second original token k, current input d (8.5x), and t=4. The strongest examples combine them, e.g. x k 3 i [d] has the max activation, and x k ? i at t=4 had precision 1.0 on 20 dev steps. No single conjunction covers it: the best simple predicate (after i, first token x, t 3-5) gets dev F1 0.26 and mass recall 0.32. An additive score of 3 or more of the 5 cues reaches mass recall 0.58 but precision only 0.20. Many activations are weak and come from other contexts.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=x (+7.20), prev_tok=i (+6.70), orig0=n (+3.71), prev2_tok=3 (+2.91), orig1=k (+2.80), t=4 (+2.76). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.82), phase=2 (-2.92), prev3_tok=- (-2.87), orig0=d (-2.22).
